steps.text: Place a large soup pot over medium heat. Add beef; cook and stir until crumbly and no longer pink, about 8 minutes. Stir in onion, celery, and bell pepper; cook until beef is browned, about 8 minutes more. Drain excess grease.
Stir diced tomatoes, water, tomato juice, bouillon cubes, chili powder, and brown sugar into beef mixture. Cover the pot, reduce heat, and simmer for 30 minutes.
Stir in macaroni; simmer until macaroni is tender, 10 to 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Wisconsin Blue Ribbon Chili
raw_recipe.description: This Wisconsin blue-ribbon chili recipe is mild, sweet, tomatoey, and full of macaroni noodles. It makes a hearty pot in one hour from start to finish.
raw_recipe.name: Wisconsin Blue Ribbon Chili

review.reviewBody: Definitely easy, and very mild. I personally added a lot more seasoning but I was using a full lb of pasta, so that may be why it needed more flavoring. I forgot the red bell pepper so I went without. I also added in more chili powder and some cumin. A+ for ease!

I make this chili a little different everytime I do it but everytime I make it everyone from the 6 year old to the 90 year old love it. Some of my favorite adaptations: -*Better than Boullion paste instead of the cubes*-Add beans (I use pinto, black, and kidney) -Half ground beef/half venison or Buffalo -For larger groups or leftovers leave out water and cook pasta separately; add as you would a topping before eating Speaking of toppings: Shredded cheddar or Colby jack sour cream oyster crackers or mini saltines Enjoy!

My family loves this one. I find it WAY too salty with all that bouillon so I just use 2. My kids don't like lots of spice so I cut the chili powder in half (though I think it would be good with both tablespoons). I also double the noodles (no change to the liquids). That way it's more like a beefaroni. We often serve it with cheese to sprinkle over the top.
It's a pretty flexible recipe. I've used other tomato-based items (such as spaghetti sauce or tomato paste) that was in my fridge in place of the juice (and just water it down if it isn't a runny kind). Or I vary the veggies (more peppers, adding mushrooms, that sort of thing) with what I have on hand.

So this was a hit! I alternated golden kernel corn instead of the red pepper. I also added diced celery & turkey sausage crumbles to elevate it. I added in white chili beans and decided to opt in for the elbow macaroni. A dollop of sour cream & sprinkle some sharp cheddar on top 
Sent enough home for everyone & ate it for dinner 2 nights in a row. This is a favorite for sure!
So easy to make and so delish. I added two 15oz cans of kidney beans as well. Definitely a great recipe for a cool Autumn evening!!
Very good.I didn't have tomato juice do I subbed 3 oz of paste and a cup of water. Loved the flavor of this chili. Sweet with a subtle kick. I did add 1 tbs of garlic powder to the meat (turkey).
Delicious! I added more noodles and 1 can of mild chili beans. Will definitely make this again!

I live all my life in WI. and 82 old. This is my chili except add 2 cans of chili beans with sauce. Also add all the spices plus others for a little heat. Add brown sugar to sweeten the taste and a little liquid smoke.
I used Ro*Tel Original diced tomatoes to spice it up. Loved this recipe.

In SE Wisconsin, all our parents made the same kind of chili. Kind of a glorified tomato soup and not spicy at all. Browned hamburger, canned tomatoes, tomato soup, kidney beans and macaroni. Seasoned with a little chili powder S & P and bay leaves.

The PHOTO clearly shows RED KIDNEY BEANS but the recipe doesn't mention them. I added 3 small cans to the mix. (Drained) Overall, it wasn't too bad. but there's clearly something different about the taste. I may have added a little too much green/red/yellow peppers. The taste was definitely different. Good, but different than what I'm used to.
I COOKED THE ELBOW NOODLES IN A SEPARATE POT SO I DELETED THE WATER IN THE MIX. PLUS I ADDED MORE OF THEM. IT WAS GREAT, JUST WHAT I NEEDED.

I cooked it in the instant pot. half the meat, doubled the veggies, half the brown sugar, no bullion cubs, used low sodium chicken base and a 1T worcestershire sauce, used fresh peeled tomatoes and no tomato juice, added some powdered garlic and cumin. cooked 10 min on high pressure with natural release but the macaroni was a little over done. may try it on low pressure or do fast release next time. it was very good. great recipe to modify with what's on hand

I was slightly skeptical about adding macaroni to chili but it worked! This is the best tasting chili recipe I've ever made. However, I did make a couple changes. Starting with the meat, I used chunks of stewing meat instead of ground beef. Doing this will alter the steps, as the meat needs about 2+ hours to simmer. So you would want to hold off on the vegetables until the meat is tender. Second I replaced the tomato juice with tomato sauce Other than that, The end product is amazing. I already want to make it again!

While this may not be my favorite chili - it is really good!! I love that it’s different than all the normal “chili” recipes! I love that it’s a little sweet! I love the red bell pepper! I love the play on goulash with the noodles! We did reduce the beef bullion cubes and added a can of drained, red kidney beans. We agree! This will get made again! Loved this take on chili! Thank you WI!

I've lived in Texas for over 40 years, so it is not what a Texan would call "chili". However, I was born and raised in Wisconsin for 25 years, and by adding a can of kidney beans, it reminds me of the chili I still long for on occasion that Mama used to make.
